entries.note:
The runner takes the root record and a root-relative file and re-confines it through resolveInRoot immediately before the spawn, passing that resolved path; it never trusts a caller-supplied absolute path. Argv is literal after substituting only ${file}/${entry}; no shell, stdin closed, cwd = root, the sidecar's shell environment. The child is its own POSIX process group, so timeout and oversized output kill the whole tree (taskkill /T /F on Windows), close the pipes and wait for the exit before rejecting (review finding 4). The window between this resolution and the producer's own open cannot be closed for a path-taking executable; spec 074 and KI-037 state it.

Ported from `orchestrator/server/formats.mjs` with F156 (spec 129); nothing in this workspace spawns a project's command from JavaScript any more. The re-confinement of `${file}` is `red_project::preview::run_declared`'s, which resolves the asked path and hands this runner the ABSOLUTE one; `formats-hardening.test.mjs` drives that through the route, which is where a caller reaches it.

The BOUND was got wrong in the port and corrected 2026-09-14 (F156h): the deadline applied to `child.wait()` alone, and the reader threads were then joined, which blocks until every holder of the pipe closes it — so a producer leaving a background child holding stdout answered minutes late or never. Node's `close` needs the exit AND the streams ended, and the JS timer refused at `timeoutMs` regardless; this waits for the same two things, and on the refusal kills the group and then tells the readers to stop, which is `child.stdout.destroy()` by another name. `max_bytes` is enforced per chunk for the same reason — it is a bound on memory, not a verdict on a buffer already collected. The shell environment is composed HERE rather than by a caller, because composing it in one caller made the two halves of an availability check read different PATHs.
